#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Assemble index.html. usage: build.py <out.html> <paramsJSON file> [reportJSON file]"""
import json, re, sys, os
here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
def rd(p): return open(os.path.join(here, p), encoding='utf-8').read()
out = sys.argv[1]
params = json.loads(rd(sys.argv[2])) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else {}
report = json.loads(rd(sys.argv[3])) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else {}
policy = report.get('policy', 'policy3.js')
strat = rd('parts/head.js') + rd('parts/' + policy) + rd('parts/tail.js')
strat, n = re.subn(r'/\*PARAMS\*/[\s\S]*?/\*END\*/', lambda m: json.dumps(params, separators=(', ', ': ')), strat)
assert n == 1
sim = rd('sim.js')
main = rd('main.js')
def sub(s, key, val):
    assert key in s, key
    return s.replace(key, val)
main = sub(main, '"__STRATEGY_SUMMARY__"', json.dumps(report.get('summary', '')))
main = sub(main, '0/*__SEEDS_TESTED__*/', json.dumps(report.get('seedsTested', 0)))
main = sub(main, 'null/*__MEAN_SCORE__*/', json.dumps(report.get('meanScore', None)))
main = sub(main, '/*__SIMPLIFICATIONS__*/', ', '.join(json.dumps(x) for x in report.get('simplifications', [])))
main = sub(main, 'false/*__TESTED__*/', 'true' if report.get('testedInBrowser') else 'false')
main = sub(main, 'null/*__FPS__*/', json.dumps(report.get('measuredFps', None)))
for name, src in (('strategy', strat), ('sim', sim), ('main', main)):
    assert '</script' not in src.lower(), name
html = rd('template.html')
html = sub(html, '/*__STRATEGY__*/', strat.strip('\n'))
html = sub(html, '/*__SIM__*/', sim.strip('\n'))
html = sub(html, '/*__MAIN__*/', main.strip('\n'))
open(out, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(html)
print('wrote', out, len(html), 'bytes')

  "policy": "policy4.js",
  "summary": "Look-ahead (model-predictive) play. createStrategy() carries an exact private copy of the rules (a shadow game) that is advanced wave by wave and cross-checked against state.tick/gold/baseHp/enemy count. Purchases are just-in-time: at each wave start the shadow simulates the known waves (current + previewed, plus stratified guesses for the next three) with the current turrets and spends gold only when that predicts leaks, on the build/upgrade with the best leak reduction per gold; everything else stays banked for interest. Every slot has a target type (cannons upstream, four flak at the end of the air lane, one frost). When the build is maxed the same look-ahead swaps turret types and, with idle gold, sells and rebuilds turrets that are mid-cooldown (a rebuilt turret fires at once). target() replays the shadow's per-shot choices: cannons and flak aim at the densest useful cluster (weighted by enemy type and progress), bolts and lances avoid overkill, frost prefers un-slowed leaders. If the shadow ever disagreed with the real game it falls back to a stateless build order and default targeting. Parameters were tuned on seeds 101-148 and 1001-1056; the reported mean is from 100 untouched seeds (5001-5100): mean 47.88 waves, min 43.7, max 52.1. About 0.8 s of CPU per game under V8.",

content.text:
`./index.html` is written and is the only file in the working directory. It was tested in a headless WebKit view, not Chrome, and nobody has listened to the audio.

## Self-check vectors
- **Vector A:** matches (`25.38`, fall tick `1035`, `166` entries, hash `82a5353d`).
- **Vector B:** matches (`10.93`, fall tick `457`, `48` entries, hash `2e8858d7`).
- The page re-runs both at load and sets `BENCH_REPORT.selfCheck` from the result.
- **Air lane length:** the vectors only reproduce with the polyline's geometric length, `2800`. The `2600` quoted in section 2.1 fails both hashes, so the sim uses `2800`.

## Strategy
- **Design:** `createStrategy()` carries an exact private copy of the rules and plays a shadow game alongside the real one.
- **Purchases:** at each wave start it simulates the known waves with the current turrets and buys only when leaks are predicted, choosing the best leak reduction per gold. The rest stays banked for interest.
- **Build:** each slot has a target type — cannons upstream, four flak near the end of the air lane, one frost.
- **Late game:** once the build is maxed, the same look-ahead swaps turret types. With idle gold it also sells and rebuilds turrets that are mid-cooldown, since a rebuilt turret fires at once.
- **Targeting:** `target()` replays the shadow's per-shot choices (cannons and flak aim at the densest useful cluster, bolts avoid overkill, frost prefers un-slowed leaders).
- **Safety:** if the shadow ever disagrees with the real game it falls back to a plain build order and default targeting. Look-ahead work is capped by a deterministic budget.

Measured in my own harness (my `rampart-sim` under V8), not the grader's engine:

| Seeds | Mean waves | Min | Max |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5001–5100 (untouched, reported in `BENCH_REPORT`) | 47.88 | 43.7 | 52.1 |
| 7001–7300 | 47.76 | 42.9 | 51.3 |

- Parameters were tuned on other seeds (101–148, 1001–1056).
- The bolts-only baseline of vector A scores 25.38 on seed 42; this strategy scores 48.63 there (fall at tick 1965, about 98.3 s into the replay).
- The shadow never went out of sync on any of these seeds.
- CPU is about 0.7–1.0 s per game on this machine.

## Page
- **Implemented in full:** board, enemies and turrets, combat visuals, leaks and the fall with desaturation, in-canvas HUD, synthesized audio, the five-state playback machine.
- **Simplifications** (also listed in `BENCH_REPORT.simplifications`):
  - `rampartSimulate` takes an optional fourth argument, a passive recorder the page uses to capture per-tick state; with three arguments it behaves as specified.
  - Stacked enemies are drawn with a small seeded sideways offset so they stay readable.
  - Health bars overlap heavily in dense late-game stacks.
  - The HUD keeps its colours after the fall while the scene goes grey.
  - The three scripts sit in `<head>` so `<body>` holds only the canonical markup.

## Browser testing
- **What I ran:** the finished file in a headless WKWebView (Safari's engine, real WebGL2) with scripted frames. The sandbox would not run Chrome, Firefox or Electron.
- **Verified there:**
  - no page errors;
  - countdown, play/pause, speed pills, scrubbing, re-fire and end-of-timeline behaviour, driven through hand-pumped frames;
  - identical pixels for the same `simTime` after scrubbing away and back;
  - dock geometry and DOM contract;
  - screenshots at 1280×650 and 1920×1080, including the leak and fall sequences and a no-fall seed.
- **Not verified:**
  - behaviour in Chrome;
  - how the audio mix sounds — the audio paths ran without errors, but nobody listened;
  - real vsync frame rate. `measuredFps: 91` is render throughput in that WebKit view (about 6–11 ms per frame at 1920×1080, device pixel ratio 2), not a Chrome reading.
